result: Review: 99.7% of a libniji dynamic start is ld.so; 298 symbolic relocations cost 493,648 (59%), 277 of libc.so.6's 285 names are its own; prototype binding them (malloc family kept) takes the empty main 742,449 -> 328,846; per-lookup 1,373 vs ~600 and per-object 93,819 vs 11,958 against glibc 2.39; 7 ranked briefs, target ~180k after them

rulings.item: LIBC-SELF-BIND: link libc.so.6 so its own function references bind locally (malloc family and probe-settled families stay preemptible, exported data stays symbolic)
rulings.recommendation: yes, after per-family reference probes; prototype measured -413,603 instructions per empty start with malloc replacement unchanged
yes, after the RELR loop gets the window treatment

informational: libniji's system libc6-dev (21.5, 21.6) ships no .h files: a swapped root loses /usr/include/stdio.h
start-up is ~0.03% of pass-2 CPU (challenge #7390): it matters for printf-loop and process-heavy workloads, not our gate
a static glibc empty main runs 133,200 user instructions, more than its dynamic one (99,262)

impact.what: review and briefs only; no libniji behaviour changes
7 briefs: LIBC-SELF-BIND, LD-LOOKUP-COST, LD-PHDR-ONCE, LD-OBJECT-ONCE, LD-RELR-LOOP, LD-VERSIONS-ONCE, LD-START-MAPS
prototype (not shipped): libc self-references bound, empty dynamic main, Zen 1, user instructions

improvement: a start-up attribution kit (callgrind in a swapped root plus a like-for-like native count of valgrind's client environment) is reusable: put cg.sh/meas.sh/stcount.c in validation/ so every loader story profiles in minutes
next_step: coordinator rules on LIBC-SELF-BIND and RELR; LD-LOOKUP-COST, LD-PHDR-ONCE and LD-VERSIONS-ONCE can start now
